facts.statement: Kazuhiko Sakurai, Masaichi Kimura, and Takayuki Katoh described the genus and species Hokkaidornis abashiriensis in 2008 based on a semi-complete skeleton lacking the skull.
facts.quote: In 2008, Kazuhiko Sakurai, Masaichi Kimura and Takayuki Katoh described the new genus and species Hokkaidornis abashiriensis, using as holotype the specimen AMP 44, a semi-complete skeleton lacking the skull.

facts.statement: The first remains of Hokkaidornis were found in the Late Oligocene sediments of the Tokoro Formation near the city of Abashiri on the island of Hokkaido.
facts.quote: The first Hokkaidornis remains were discovered in sediments dated from the Late Oligocene of the Tokoro Formation, near the city of Abashiri, in the Japanese island of Hokkaido

facts.statement: Hokkaidornis was a large-bodied plotopterid with an estimated height of 1.3 meters and a length of 1.7 meters.
facts.quote: Hokkaidornis was a large-bodied plotopterid, with estimated height of 1.3 m and length of 1.7 m

facts.statement: The radius of Hokkaidornis was flattened like in other plotopterids, while its ulna was the largest known for the group.
facts.quote: The radius was flattened like in other plotopterid, while the ulna was the largest known for plotopterids.

facts.statement: The pelvis of Hokkaidornis shared similarities with those of modern anhingas.
facts.quote: The pelvis shared similarities with those of modern anhingas.

facts.statement: The tarsometatarsus of Hokkaidornis was quite similar to those of modern-day penguins.
facts.quote: The tarsometatarsus was more robust and less elongated than in Phocavis, but was nearly undistinguishable to that of the paratype of C. hexeris, and quite similar to those of modern-day penguins.

facts.statement: Hokkaidornis lived during the Chattian stage, from 27.3 to 23.04 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Chattian to Chattian (27.3 to 23.04 million years ago)
